Luis: In the Q&A you emphasized mission and positioning. Can you give one succinct sentence the marketing team can use for the website that isn't just "inference platform"?

Elena (CEO): Use this: "Redwood Inference: predictable, economical LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments." It's tight and highlights the three deployment promises.

Tara (Sales): How do we handle customers who ask "why not the big cloud vendor?"

Maya (VP Product): Answer: Cloud vendors offer model access but tradeoffs in cost predictability and ops. We offer the runtime + controls that turn model capabilities into production-grade features with measurable unit economics.

Ravi (CTO): Technical add: call out our strengths: continuous batching, KV/prefix cache, and kernel selection. These are the levers that yield better latency/cost than naive hosting.

Luis: Any quick competitor dos-and-donts for messaging?

Elena (CEO): Dos: lead with numbers (p99, $/M tokens, uptime). Don't say "we have the best models" as a claim. Donts: vague performance claims or feature lists without outcomes.

Tara: For positioning doc, sales wants one line vs three competitor archetypes. Example?

Maya: CloudVendor = wide model catalog, infra lock-in. ModelAPI = simple access, variable economics. Self-host = lower headline cost but high ops tax and quality tuning burden. Our line: unified runtime + observable economics + enterprise controls.

Ravi: Follow-up tech ask: can we produce a 1-slide benchmark showing cost per 1M tokens vs a popular self-hosted stack? I can run a quick internal benchmark.

Elena (CEO): Do it. Action items: Ravi to run benchmark by Wed, Luis to draft the website headline by Tue, Maya to assemble competitor one-liner by Wed, Tara to get sales playbook snippet by Fri. I'll review proofs before publishing.
